name: Groundnut Rosette Virus
description: A devastating viral disease complex of groundnut causing severe stunting and leaf distortion. It is transmitted by aphids and is one of the most important groundnut diseases in sub-Saharan Africa, causing yield losses up to 100% in severe epidemics.
symptoms: Chlorotic mottling and mosaic patterns on young leaves
Leaf distortion with downward curling of leaflets
Dark green leaf blades with pale veins (chlorotic rosette)
Plants becoming bushy with shortened internodes
Pegs failing to penetrate soil or pods failing to develop
causes: Groundnut rosette virus complex (GRV + its satellite RNA + GRAV)
Aphid populations building up during dry spells
Groundnut volunteers and wild legumes as virus reservoirs
Late planting coinciding with peak aphid populations
seasonality: Dry season to early rainy season (aphid peak)
treatments: Remove and destroy infected plants immediately
Control aphid vectors with systemic insecticides
Apply neem oil or insecticidal soap for aphid control
prevention: Plant early to avoid peak aphid populations
Use neem-based seed treatment before planting
Rogue out infected plants as soon as symptoms appear
Remove volunteer groundnut plants and wild legumes near fields
Intercrop with maize or sorghum to reduce aphid landing
